explanation: Single body falling at 60 m/s with gravity 30 and dt=1/30 triggers 71 substeps in one step, and velocity grows from -60 to -66 (gain of 6) instead of expected g*dt=1 gain to -61. Position falls only ~2.1, so PE drop cannot account for KE jump, producing net energy gain ~315 J that exceeds the 10%+5 J tolerance with zero controller work. Likely cause is gravity (or dt scaling) mishandled inside the fast-motion substep loop, adding excess velocity per substep.
